title: The Hidden Relationship Between Product Strategy and UX Design
text: Medium The Hidden Relationship Between Product Strategy and UX Design | by Gul Ahmed Shah | Nov, 2026 | Medium Sitemap Open in app Sign up Sign in Medium Logo Get app Write Search Sign up Sign in Member-only story Product Strategy UX Design Product Management User Experience Design Leadership The Hidden Relationship Between Product Strategy and UX Design Gul Ahmed Shah 18 min read · 3 hours ago -- Listen Share Stop treating them as separate phases. Here is how aligning business goals with user intent builds products that actually scale. I still remember the exact moment I realized our product team was fundamentally broken. It was a rainy Tuesday afternoon in a cramped conference room in San Francisco. The air conditioning was humming a steady, monotonous tune. The whiteboard was covered in a chaotic mess of sticky notes, half-erased diagrams, and conflicting priorities. On one side of the table sat the product management team. On the other side sat the design team. The tension in the room was thick enough to cut with a knife. We were debating the roadmap for our core SaaS platform. The product manager was passionately arguing for a new feature. He explained that our churn rate was climbing, and the data suggested that adding a complex, gamified loyalty program would increase user retention by fifteen percent. He had the spreadsheets to prove it. He had the executive buy-in. The lead designer pushed back immediately. She argued that adding a gamified loyalty program would introduce massive cognitive friction into an already complicated onboarding flow. She explained that our users were busy professionals who wanted to get in, complete their task, and get out. They did not want to play games. She had the usability testing recordings to prove it. She had the user quotes. -- -- Written by Gul Ahmed Shah 7 followers · 2 following UX/UI designer, developer, and writer exploring thoughtful design and modern software.
